item.title: A Model of the Attention Economy: Data, Platforms, and Discovery
item.headline: Better ad targeting can change who benefits over time
item.summary: Free online services depend on advertising, but better targeting need not keep raising their revenue. In this theoretical model, improved targeting initially lifts ad revenue; as consumers discover better-matched competitors, advertisers become less willing to pay. The reversal illustrates a possible mechanism, not a measured effect of a privacy law.

evidence.question: How do advertising and product discovery interact over time?
evidence.method: Mathematical equilibrium model and numerical policy experiments.
evidence.limitations: Stylized preferences fix product prices; the baseline omits strategic platform interaction.

explainer.finding: Better targeting can raise advertising revenue initially but lower it later.
explainer.method: The model links ad auctions, product discovery and investment in free services.
explainer.meaning: Imagine shoe ads helping you discover several suitable shops. Each shop must then compete with the others for your spending.
explainer.limits: This is theory, not a forecast. Discovery without ads and personalized pricing could alter the results.
